subject: Bayesian spatial modelling with INLA using two different likelihoods of data with unequal sample size

messages.author: cdaedda7d73defe4
messages.subject: Bayesian spatial modelling with INLA using two different likelihoods of data with unequal sample size
parts:
Hi Dear INLA users,

I have some questions about the Bayesian modeling based on INLA using multiple likelihoods.

When reading the following two papers:

- Martins TG, Simpson D, Lindgren F, Rue H (2013) Bayesian computing with INLA: New features. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis 67:68–83. doi: 10.1016/j.csda.2013.04.014
 
- Illian JB, Martino S, Sørbye SH, et al (2013) Fitting complex ecological point process models with integrated nested Laplace approximation. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 4:305–315. doi: 10.1111/2041-21...@10.1111/(ISSN)2041-210X.STATSTOO,

I found out that it is possible to fit Bayesian models with INLA using multiple likelihoods. For all the cas studies above, the sample sizes of the data implying the two likelihoods are equal.
A typical example in forestry is the marked point process models (see Illian et al. 2013), where in addition to the observed individuals (i.e. spatial locations of a species, which is modelled by point process likelihood), we have additional information related to the health status of each species (modeled by binomial likelihood) or the diameter of each species (which can be modeled by Gaussian likelihood).

However, let's suppose that, the data available for the second likelihood is aggregated in grid cells (e.g. a regular lattice), such that its sample size (say m) is less than the one of the first data (say n), of which individuals are observed at each spatial location. As example, see the Dorazio's approach proposed in Species Distribution Models (Dorazio RM (2014) Accounting for imperfect detection and survey bias in statistical analysis of presence‐only data. Global Ecology and Biogeography 23:1472–1484. doi: 10.1111/geb.12216) , which includes two likelihoods: Poisson point process likelihood for the presence-only data and Poisson likelihood for the point-counts (aggregated data in grid cells).

My questions is that:

- Is it possible to apply the Dorazio approach with INLA using the multiple likelihoods framework of Martins et al. (2013)? And how to do it (any attempt of code) ?

- Can the INLA handle the sampling bias (using thinned point process models) along with imperfect detection issue as proposed in Dorazio (2014) ?

Any answers or clarifications will be very appreciated.

Best.
